summary: This function scans the blog directory for MDX files and extracts metadata from the frontmatter of each post. It normalizes the data by resolving permalinks (using either a custom slug or the folder structure), fixing relative image paths, and converting fields to the correct types, then returns a filtered array of structured blog post metadata objects.

explanations.51: require.context tells Webpack to load all MDX files from the blog directory at build time, creating a special object where you can retrieve files by their path.
explanations.57: We're casting the loaded post to an object with a frontMatter property so TypeScript knows what shape the data has.
explanations.59: We extract the folder name from the file path by removing the /index.mdx part and the leading ./ that Webpack adds.
explanations.62: If the post has a custom slug in its frontmatter, we use that as the permalink; otherwise we fall back to deriving it from the folder structure.
explanations.63: The slug might already start with a slash, so we preserve that; if not, we add /blog/ prefix to create the full URL path.
explanations.71: Image paths that start with ./ are relative to the blog post's folder, so we convert them to absolute paths that start from the root.
explanations.79: Boolean() converts truthy/falsy values to explicit true or false, since draft might be undefined or a string.
explanations.82: We use || [] to provide an empty array as a default if tags aren't defined in the frontmatter, preventing undefined from appearing in the metadata.
explanations.89: filter(Boolean) removes any falsy entries (though with the current structure, this is mainly a safety check).
